questions.q: A payment shows 'Paid' in Payables but is not reflected in the GL cash account. What does this most likely indicate?
options: The cash was never actually transferred to the supplier
An accounting-pipeline step hasn't completed yet, not that money is missing
The supplier's bank account is invalid
The payment was accidentally deleted
questions.explain: A 'Paid' status confirms the payment is real and complete; the issue is that the related journal entry has not yet reached or posted in General Ledger.

questions.q: What are the two separate steps between a subledger transaction and a posted GL journal entry?
options: Validate, then Pay
Approve, then Validate
Reconcile, then Close
Create Accounting (generates the journal), then Transfer to GL (moves it into General Ledger)
questions.explain: Create Accounting generates the journal entry (Draft or Final mode); Transfer to GL separately moves a Final-mode entry into General Ledger as an unposted journal, which still needs posting.

questions.q: In this ticket, what did checking the payment's accounting status reveal?
options: It showed Accounted – Final, meaning Create Accounting had already run successfully
It was still in Draft mode
It showed an error status
It had not been accounted at all
questions.explain: The payment was Accounted – Final, confirming the journal entry existed; the gap was that it hadn't yet been transferred to GL.

questions.q: What was the actual root cause of the journal entry not appearing in GL?
options: A disabled account combination
The period was closed
The payment was accounted after that day's nightly Transfer Journal Entries to GL run had already completed
The supplier record was inactive
questions.explain: The entry went Final after the scheduled nightly transfer had already run, so it was correctly waiting for the next scheduled run — not lost or in error.

questions.q: Why does the resolution note explicitly say 'no data correction was needed'?
options: Because that phrase is required on every ticket
Because the fix was simply running an existing program manually — nothing about the underlying data or setup was actually wrong
Because the ticket was closed without any action
Because the payment had to be reversed
questions.explain: The resolution clarifies that this was purely a timing gap resolved by running Transfer Journal Entries to GL manually, not a correction to incorrect data or setup.
